extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and PTAB litigators (practitioners before the PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for when the USPTO/PTAB may exercise its discretion to deny institution of post‑grant proceedings (IPR/PGR) when there is a parallel proceeding. Covers the historic Fintiv factors, Sotera stipulations, interim‑memorandum rules, and the March 2025 Workload Management procedures for discretionary‑denial briefing and decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — stay existence/likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a stay exists or is likely to be granted if a proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the holistic Fintiv six‑factor framework used to decide discretionary denials when a parallel co‑pending proceeding exists; a court stay or likely stay weighs in favor of denying PTAB institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — proximity of court trial date
rubrics_metrics.description: The proximity of the court’s trial date to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the district court's trial is near the PTAB's projected deadline for a final written decision, that proximity is a factor favoring discretionary denial; the Board may consider median time‑to‑trial statistics as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — investment in parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of time, resources, and work already expended in the parallel forum can favor denying PTAB institution to avoid duplicative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — overlap of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition’s grounds substantially overlap with issues in the parallel litigation (e.g., same prior art/arguments), that weighs toward discretionary denial to avoid duplicative adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — identity of parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parties are the same in both forums, the factor supports denying institution because the parallel action may resolve the dispute; identity of parties is a relevant overlap consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor — other circumstances (including merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the merits of the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch‑all factor including considerations not captured elsewhere; while strength of the merits is considered, compelling merits alone are not dispositive under the updated guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sotera stipulation (petitioner stipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sotera stipulation is a petitioner’s stipulation that 'if IPR is instituted, they will not pursue in the District Court Litigation any ground raised or that could have been reasonably raised in an IPR.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely Sotera stipulations are highly relevant and, under the earlier Sotera decision, made the fourth Fintiv factor strongly favor not exercising discretion to deny institution; under current guidance they are important to the holistic assessment but not dispositive on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Procedures — ITC parallel proceeding carve‑out
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the June 22, 2022 Interim Procedures Memorandum the Board would not exercise its authority to deny institution when the parallel proceeding was an ITC proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interim Memorandum treated ITC proceedings as a basis against exercising discretionary denial; subsequent rescission of the Interim Memorandum means this is no longer a guaranteed rule but it was an express prior consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Procedures — Sotera stipulation effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Interim Procedures Memorandum, the existence of a Sotera stipulation counseled against exercising discretionary denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interim Memorandum explicitly listed timely Sotera stipulations as a circumstance where the Board would not deny institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Procedures — compelling evidence of unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Interim Procedures Memorandum, compelling evidence of unpatentability counseled against exercising discretionary denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition presented compelling evidence of unpatentability, the Board would generally proceed rather than deny institution under the Interim Memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — applicability of rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: The rescission of the Interim Procedures Memorandum applies if (1) the Board has not issued an institution decision or (2) a request for rehearing or Director Review of an institution decision was filed and is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the temporal scope in which the Interim Memorandum was rescinded and when the new guidance applies to pending matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — Fintiv factors apply to ITC as well
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fintiv factors apply when there is a parallel proceeding at the ITC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The March 24, 2025 Guidance clarified that the Board may consider the Fintiv framework even for ITC proceedings, narrowing the Interim Memorandum’s earlier carve‑out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — Sotera stipulations are relevant but not dispositive
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely‑filed Sotera stipulations are highly relevant and considered as part of the Fintiv holistic analysis, but they are not dispositive on their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with a Sotera stipulation, the Board balances multiple factors; practitioners should not assume a stipulation automatically prevents discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — consideration of median time‑to‑trial statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board can consider evidence relating to the proximity of the district court’s trial date, such as median time‑to‑trial statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical district court timing data may be submitted and weighed as part of the proximity analysis under the Fintiv factors or other discretionary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — balanced assessment including merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fintiv factors are to be considered as part of a balanced assessment, including the strength of the merits, but compelling merits are not dispositive on their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merits evidence (strength of unpatentability) is a factor but cannot alone overcome other discretionary considerations; the Board performs a holistic balancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload Management — bifurcation of institution decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution decisions are bifurcated between (i) discretionary considerations and (ii) merits and other non‑discretionary statutory considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directive separates the threshold discretionary analysis from the merits analysis; the discretionary decision is made before merit panels address institution in normal course if discretionary denial is not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload Management — decisionmakers and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director and at least three PTAB judges determine whether discretionary denial is appropriate; if appropriate, the Director issues a decision denying institution; if not, the petition is referred to a three‑member panel for normal handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the actors and workflow for discretionary denials — a multi‑judge/Director review rather than immediate three‑member panel institution decision in cases with discretionary issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary denial briefing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a brief explaining applicable bases for discretionary denial within 2 months of the PTAB entering a Notice of Filing Date Accorded; the petitioner may file an opposition brief no later than 1 month after the filing date of the patent owner’s brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are given specific windows to submit discretionary denial briefs as part of the bifurcated process; adhere to these timing rules to preserve arguments for the Director/judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing word limits for discretionary briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretionary denial briefing has a limit of 14,000 words and a reply brief has a limit of 5,600 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Workload Management Memorandum imposes word‑count caps on the discretionary owner brief and petitioner reply/opposition; practitioners must conform to these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload Management — permitted considerations parties may address
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are permitted (but not limited) to address specific considerations including: whether PTAB or another forum already adjudicated validity; changes in law/new judicial precedent since claim issuance; strength of the unpatentability challenge; extent of petition’s reliance on expert testimony; settled expectations of the parties (e.g., how long claims have been in force); compelling economic, public health, or national security interests; and any other considerations bearing on the Director’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This non‑exhaustive list defines typical topics parties should address in discretionary briefing; it signals that factual, legal, policy, and equitable considerations can all bear on the Director’s exercise of discretion.
